mainTopic: Taking back a deathbed gift: a קנין, the wording 'in life and in death,' and who must prove the giver was sick
overview: This amud first settles how far an earlier rule reaches: a שכיב מרע who gave a gift with a formal קנין cannot take it back. רב חסדא, quoting רב הונא, says this holds both for keeping the gift himself and for giving it to someone else, and a story with רב הונא shows the rule in action. Next, רב and שמואל argue about a gift document that says 'in life and in death.' רב calls it a deathbed gift, and שמואל calls it a healthy person's gift. The scholars of נהרדעא rule like רב. רבא adds that the wording 'from life' makes the gift final, but אמימר rules that the הלכה is not like רבא. Two stories follow: רב נחמן will not rule against שמואל in שמואל's town, and a woman curses רבא after he tries to trick her. Then a new משנה asks who must prove whether the giver was sick or healthy. The גמרא begins with a deed that mentions the illness but not that the giver died from it.

steps.title: A first understanding: the rule only blocks giving to someone else
steps.stepSummary: The scholars first understood that the earlier rule only stops the שכיב מרע from moving the gift to another person, but not from taking it back for himself.
steps.simpleTranslation: They understood from this: this rule only applies to giving it to another person, but for himself, no.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells us how some scholars first understood the earlier rule about a שכיב מרע who gave a gift with a קנין. This sets up a correction in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The earlier rule said he cannot take back such a gift. The scholars read it narrowly: he cannot take it away to give to someone else. But if he recovers and wants the property back for himself, they thought he can.

keyTerms.meaning: They understood from it (a first reading that may be corrected)
These words apply only to... (limits a rule)
To another person
For himself

steps.confusionAlert: This is only a first understanding. The very next step rejects it, so do not walk away thinking this is the הלכה.

phrases.english: They understood from this:
phrases.notes: "This" is the earlier rule that a שכיב מרע who made a קנין on his gift cannot take it back.

phrases.english: this applies only to giving it to another,
but for himself, it does not apply.
phrases.notes: He means: if he gets well and wants the property back for himself, they thought he could take it back.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Narrows the scope of the rule discussed just before this section.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: First reading: the קנין only stops him from moving the gift to another person, not from taking it back for himself.

steps.title: רב חסדא: the rule covers both himself and others
steps.stepSummary: רב חסדא rejects the narrow reading. He reports that רב הונא explained the rule applies both to taking it back for himself and to giving it to others.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב חסדא said to them: When רב הונא came from כופרי, he explained it: whether for himself or for others.
steps.whatsHappening: רב חסדא corrects the scholars' narrow understanding by quoting רב הונא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: According to רב הונא, once there was a קנין, the שכיב מרע cannot take the gift back at all. That holds even if he recovers and wants it for himself. The קנין makes the gift as firm as a healthy person's gift.

keyTerms.meaning: When he came (from another place)
כופרי, a place name
He explained it
Whether... or... (both cases)

steps.whatToRemember: A שכיב מרע who gave a gift with a קנין cannot take it back, not for himself and not for someone else.

phrases.english: Rav Chisda said to them:
When Rav Huna came from Kufrei,
he explained it: whether for himself or for others.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the narrow reading given in step 1.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The limit that the rule applies only to giving to others.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: רב הונא, quoted by רב חסדא, explained that the rule covers both cases.

steps.title: A real case: רב הונא will not let him take back his gift
steps.stepSummary: A שכיב מרע made a קנין on his gift and later wanted to take it back. רב הונא told him he could not, because he did not give it the usual way people on their deathbed give.
steps.simpleTranslation: A certain man had a קנין done on his gift. He came before רב הונא. רב הונא said: What can I do for you? You did not transfer it the way people normally transfer.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells a story that shows רב הונא's rule in practice.
steps.deeperAnalysis: People on their deathbed usually give gifts by words alone, and those gifts can be taken back if they recover. This man added a formal קנין, which made the gift stronger. So רב הונא could not help him get it back.

keyTerms.meaning: They made a קנין with him (a formal act of acquisition)
What can I do for you?
You transferred ownership

phrases.english: There was a certain man from whom they made a kinyan,
phrases.notes: He was a שכיב מרע who gave a gift with a קנין, then got better and wanted it back.

phrases.english: he came before Rav Huna.
He said: What can I do for you,
since you did not transfer the way people transfer.
phrases.notes: People on their deathbed normally give by words alone. By adding a קנין, he made the gift firm.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Shows רב הונא applying the rule from step 2 in a real case.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A gift by a שכיב מרע with a קנין cannot be taken back even if he recovers.

steps.title: A gift document saying 'in life and in death': רב and שמואל disagree
steps.stepSummary: A gift document said 'in life and in death.' רב says it is a deathbed gift, which can be taken back. שמואל says it is a healthy person's gift, which cannot.
steps.simpleTranslation: There was a certain gift document in which was written 'in life and in death.' רב said: It is like the gift of a שכיב מרע. שמואל said: It is like the gift of a healthy person.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new topic: a disagreement between רב and שמואל about a gift document with mixed wording.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The words 'in death' sound like a deathbed gift that starts after he dies. The words 'in life' sound like a gift that starts now, like a healthy person's gift. The question is which words decide the type of gift.

keyTerms.meaning: A gift (here, a gift document)
In life and in death
Gift of a person on his deathbed. It takes effect at death and can be taken back if he recovers
Gift of a healthy person. It takes effect now and cannot be taken back

steps.whyThisMatters: The answer decides whether the giver can take back the gift if he recovers.

phrases.english: There was a certain gift document
in which was written "in life and in death":

phrases.aramaic: רַב אָמַר: הֲרֵי הִיא כְּמַתְּנַת שְׁכִיב מְרַע.
phrases.english: Rav said: It is like the gift of a person on his deathbed.

phrases.aramaic: וּשְׁמוּאֵל אָמַר: הֲרֵי הִיא כְּמַתְּנַת בָּרִיא.
phrases.english: And Shmuel said: It is like the gift of a healthy person.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic, still about deathbed gifts.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רב: a deathbed gift (can be taken back). שמואל: a healthy person's gift (cannot be taken back).

steps.title: רב's reasoning: 'in death' decides, and 'in life' is just a blessing
steps.stepSummary: רב reads 'in death' as the real meaning: the gift starts after death. He explains 'in life' as just a good-luck wish that the giver should live.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב said it is like the gift of a שכיב מרע: since it is written in it 'in death,' he is telling him it is after death. And what is written 'in life' is just a good sign, that he should live.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins explaining the reasoning behind רב's view.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רב, the words 'in death' show when the gift really starts: after the giver dies. That makes it a deathbed gift. The words 'in life' have no legal meaning; they are only a hopeful wish for the giver's recovery.

keyTerms.meaning: Since it is written
After death
Merely a sign (here, a good-luck wish)

phrases.aramaic: רַב אָמַר הֲרֵי הִיא כְּמַתְּנַת שְׁכִיב מְרַע –
phrases.english: Rav said it is like the gift of a person on his deathbed:
since it is written in it "in death,"
he is telling him it takes effect after death;
and that which is written "in life"
is merely a good sign, that he should live.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב אָמַר הֲרֵי הִיא כְּמַתְּנַת שְׁכִיב מְרַע מִדִּכְתִיב בָּהּ בַּמָּוֶת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the reasoning behind רב's view in step 4.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: 'In death' shows the gift starts after death. 'In life' is only a good-luck wish, so it is a deathbed gift.

steps.title: שמואל explains why it is a healthy person's gift
steps.stepSummary: שמואל reads 'in life' as the main meaning: the gift starts right now. He reads 'in death' as a way of saying the gift lasts forever.
steps.simpleTranslation: And שמואל says it is like a healthy person's gift. Since it says 'in life,' the giver means the gift starts while he is alive. And when he wrote 'and in death,' that is like saying 'from now and forever.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now gives שמואל's side, the mirror image of how רב read the same two words.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב treated 'in death' as the real meaning and 'in life' as a blessing. שמואל flips this. 'In life' is the real meaning, so the gift takes effect now. 'In death' only stresses that the gift stays with the receiver even after the giver dies, so it cannot be taken back.

keyTerms.meaning: A gift from a healthy person. It cannot be taken back.
From life, meaning the gift takes effect right now, while the giver is alive.
From now and forever, meaning a permanent gift.

phrases.aramaic: וּשְׁמוּאֵל אָמַר הֲרֵי הִיא כְּמַתְּנַת בָּרִיא –
phrases.english: And Shmuel says: it is like a healthy person's gift
since it is written in it 'in life,'
he is saying 'from life'
phrases.notes: He means the gift kicks in right now, while the giver is still alive.

phrases.english: and that which he wrote, 'and in death,'
is like one who says 'from now and forever.'

steps.triggerLanguage: וּשְׁמוּאֵל אָמַר הֲרֵי הִיא כְּמַתְּנַת בָּרִיא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives שמואל's reading of the document, in parallel to רב's reading in step 5.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: 'In life' means the gift takes effect now. 'In death' only means it is permanent, so it is a healthy person's gift and cannot be taken back.

steps.title: The scholars of נהרדעא rule like רב
steps.stepSummary: The scholars of נהרדעא decide the practical law follows רב: the gift is a deathbed gift.
steps.simpleTranslation: The scholars of נהרדעא say: the הלכה follows רב.
steps.whatsHappening: After hearing both sides, the גמרא reports the practical ruling: we follow רב.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In practice, a document saying 'in life and in death' is treated as a שכיב מרע's gift. So if the giver gets better, he can take it back.

keyTerms.meaning: The scholars of the city of נהרדעא.
The practical law follows his opinion.

steps.whatToRemember: A document saying 'in life and in death' counts as a deathbed gift, following רב.

phrases.english: The scholars of Neharde'a say:
the halakha is like Rav.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Settles the argument between רב and שמואל.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The הלכה follows רב: 'in life and in death' is a deathbed gift.

steps.title: רבא: if it says 'from life,' the receiver acquires
steps.stepSummary: רבא adds a new case. If the document says 'from life' instead of 'in life,' the gift is final.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: and if it is written in the document 'from life,' the receiver acquires the gift.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא brings a slightly different wording and says that even רב's view would not make it a deathbed gift.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'From life' clearly says the gift starts now, while the giver is alive. רבא holds that this wording is too strong to explain away as a blessing. So the receiver keeps the gift even though the document also mentions death.

keyTerms.meaning: He acquired, meaning the receiver owns it for good.

phrases.english: Rava said:
And if it is written in it 'from life,' he acquires.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רָבָא וְאִי כְּתִיב בַּהּ מֵחַיִּים קְנָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Limits the ruling like רב to the wording 'in life'. With 'from life,' the gift is final.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: If the document says 'from life' (and in death), the receiver acquires and the giver cannot take it back.

steps.title: אמימר: the הלכה is not like רבא
steps.stepSummary: אמימר rules against רבא. Even 'from life' does not make the gift final.
steps.simpleTranslation: אמימר said: the הלכה is not like רבא.
steps.whatsHappening: אמימר rejects רבא's new case as the practical law.
steps.deeperAnalysis: According to אמימר, as long as the document also mentions death, it is still a deathbed gift, even if it says 'from life.' So the giver can take it back if he recovers.

keyTerms.meaning: The law is not like this.

phrases.english: Ameimar said:
The halakha is not like Rava.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר אַמֵּימָר לֵית הִלְכְתָא כְּווֹתֵיהּ דְּרָבָא
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: רבא's ruling that 'from life' makes the gift final.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: A document that also mentions death is still a deathbed gift, even with the word 'from life'.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The הלכה is not like רבא. Even wording like 'from life' does not make the gift final when the document also mentions death.

steps.title: רב אשי: isn't that obvious?
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי asks אמימר why he needed to say this. We already know the הלכה follows רב.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אשי said to אמימר: that is obvious! The scholars of נהרדעא already said the הלכה follows רב.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי challenges אמימר's statement as unnecessary.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If we already rule like רב, that a document mentioning death is a deathbed gift, then of course we do not follow רבא. So why did אמימר need to say it?

keyTerms.meaning: It is obvious, so why say it?

phrases.english: Rav Ashi said to Ameimar:
It is obvious, since the scholars of Neharde'a say:
the halakha is like Rav!

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַב אָשֵׁי לְאַמֵּימָר פְּשִׁיטָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions why אמימר's ruling in step 9 was needed.
steps.kashyaTarget: אמימר's statement that the הלכה is not like רבא.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Ruling like רב (step 7) already means that mentioning death makes it a deathbed gift, so אמימר's statement adds nothing.

steps.title: We might have thought רב agrees with 'from life'
steps.stepSummary: The answer: without אמימר, we could have thought רב agrees with רבא when the document says 'from life'.
steps.simpleTranslation: You might have said that with 'from life,' רב agrees the gift is final. So אמימר teaches us that this is not so.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers רב אשי's question by showing what new point אמימר is teaching.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב explained 'in life' as only a blessing. But 'from life' is harder to explain away, so maybe רב would agree there. אמימר teaches that even then, the mention of death makes it a deathbed gift.

keyTerms.meaning: You might have said (a mistaken idea we need to correct).
Agrees.
It teaches us (that this is not so).

steps.whatToRemember: The final law: once the document mentions death, it is a deathbed gift, even if it also says 'from life.'

phrases.english: You might have said that with 'from life,' Rav agrees;
so it teaches us otherwise.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַהוּ דְּתֵימָא מֵחַיִּים מוֹדֵי רַב קָא מַשְׁמַע לַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רב אשי's challenge from step 10.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Shows that the statement teaches something new.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: We might have thought רב agrees that 'from life' makes the gift final.
steps.terutzMaskana: Even with 'from life,' רב treats it as a deathbed gift, and the הלכה follows him.

steps.title: רב נחמן sends a case away from שמואל's town
steps.stepSummary: A man brought his case to רב נחמן in נהרדעא. רב נחמן sent him to רבי ירמיה בר אבא in שום טמיא, because in שמואל's town he could not rule like רב.
steps.simpleTranslation: A certain man came before רב נחמן in נהרדעא. רב נחמן sent him to רבי ירמיה בר אבא in שום טמיא. He said: here is שמואל's place. How can we rule like רב here?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells a story that shows how the ruling like רב worked in practice.
steps.deeperAnalysis: נהרדעא was שמואל's town, where people followed שמואל's rulings. So רב נחמן would not rule like רב there, against שמואל. Instead, he sent the case to a different judge in another place.

keyTerms.meaning: Place, here meaning the town where a rabbi's rulings are followed.
He sent him.

steps.whyThisMatters: It shows respect for a rabbi's authority in his own town. Even when the הלכה follows רב, a judge would not rule against שמואל in שמואל's place.

phrases.english: There was a certain man who came
before Rav Nachman in Neharde'a.

phrases.aramaic: שַׁדְּרֵיהּ לְקַמֵּיהּ דְּרַבִּי יִרְמְיָה בַּר אַבָּא
phrases.english: He sent him before Rabbi Yirmeya bar Abba
in Shum Tamya.
phrases.notes: שום טמיא is the name of a place.

phrases.english: He said: here is Shmuel's place;
how can we act like Rav?!

steps.triggerLanguage: הָהוּא דַּאֲתָא לְקַמֵּיהּ דְּרַב נַחְמָן לִנְהַרְדְּעָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Shows how the ruling like רב (step 7) was carried out in שמואל's town.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: In שמואל's place, a judge does not rule like רב against שמואל. Instead, the case is sent to a judge somewhere else.

steps.title: A woman loses her case before רבא and keeps pestering him
steps.stepSummary: A woman came to רבא, and he ruled against her based on his own position. She would not accept it and kept bothering him.
steps.simpleTranslation: A certain woman came before רבא. רבא ruled in her case according to his own teaching. She kept pestering him.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells a story showing רבא putting his own ruling into practice. The woman does not accept the outcome, which sets up the next part of the story.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבא had ruled that wording like 'from life' makes the gift final, so the giver cannot take it back. Here he applies that ruling to a real case. אמימר, a later rabbi, would rule that the הלכה is not like him. The woman's constant complaining is the problem the rest of the story deals with.

keyTerms.meaning: According to his own ruling or teaching
Bothering or pestering
Before him, meaning she came to his court

phrases.english: A certain woman who came before Rava,
Rava ruled for her according to his own teaching.
phrases.notes: This is רבא's ruling from earlier: wording like 'from life' makes the gift final, so she could not take it back.

phrases.english: She kept pestering him.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Shows רבא acting on his own ruling from Step 8, after the גמרא discussed אמימר's disagreement with it.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבא ruled in a real case that the gift was final, following his own position.

steps.title: רבא has his scribe write a ruling with a hidden signal
steps.stepSummary: רבא tells his scribe רב פפא to write a ruling for the woman. The ruling includes a phrase that quietly signals it is only a trick.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said to רב פפא son of רב חנן, his scribe: Go write a ruling for her, and write in it: 'He may hire at their expense or deceive them.'
steps.whatsHappening: רבא tries to get rid of the woman by giving her a written ruling that seems to favor her. He hides a signal in it so any court would know it is not real.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The phrase 'hire at their expense or deceive them' comes from a משנה about workers who quit in the middle of a job. In that case, the employer may trick them into coming back. By putting this phrase in the document, רבא signals that this paper is a trick too, and that his real ruling has not changed.

keyTerms.meaning: His scribe
He may hire replacements at their expense
He may deceive them

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ לְרַב פָּפָּא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב חָנָן – סָפְרֵיהּ:
phrases.english: He said to Rav Pappa son of Rav Chanan, his scribe:
Go, write for her,
and write in it:
"He may hire at their expense, or deceive them."
phrases.notes: This line is from a משנה in בבא מציעא 75b about workers who quit; רבא used it as a hidden signal that this paper was a trick.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ לְרַב פָּפָּא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב חָנָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Shows רבא's response to the woman's pestering from Step 13.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבא gave her a document that looked like a ruling in her favor but carried a hidden sign that it was a trick.

steps.title: The woman sees the trick and curses רבא, and the curse comes true
steps.stepSummary: The woman understands she is being tricked and curses רבא that his ship should sink. He tries to fulfill the curse by soaking his clothes, but his ship sinks anyway.
steps.simpleTranslation: She said: May his ship sink! You are deceiving me! They dipped רבא's clothes in water, and even so he was not saved from the sinking.
steps.whatsHappening: The story ends. The woman catches the trick and curses רבא. Even though he tries to soften the curse, it still comes true.
steps.deeperAnalysis: She recognized the phrase 'deceive them' and realized the document was meant to fool her. רבא had his clothes dipped in water so the 'sinking' would happen in a harmless way. It did not work, and his ship really sank. This ends the story and the topic before the new משנה begins.

keyTerms.meaning: May his ship sink
Deceiving or tricking
His clothes
Sinking

phrases.english: She said: May his ship sink!
You are deceiving me!
They dipped Rava's clothes in water,
phrases.notes: He hoped the curse of 'sinking' would come true in this harmless way instead.

phrases.english: and even so, he was not saved from the sinking.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the story begun in Steps 13–14.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The woman saw through the trick, and her curse came true despite רבא's effort to soften it.
steps.whatToRemember: רבא stood by his own ruling that wording like 'from life' makes a gift final. But the practical הלכה, following אמימר (step 9), is not like רבא.

steps.title: New משנה: a deed that does not say the giver was dying, according to רבי מאיר
steps.stepSummary: The deed does not say the giver was a שכיב מרע. He claims he was sick, so he can take the gift back. The receivers say he was healthy. רבי מאיר says the giver must prove he was sick.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: If he did not write in the deed that he was a שכיב מרע, and he says 'I was a שכיב מרע' while they say 'You were healthy,' he must bring proof that he was a שכיב מרע. These are the words of רבי מאיר.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins. It presents a disagreement over whether the giver was sick or healthy, and gives רבי מאיר's view on who must prove it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A gift from a שכיב מרע can be taken back if he recovers, but a healthy person's gift is final. Since the deed does not say he was sick, רבי מאיר puts the burden of proof on the giver. He must show he was a שכיב מרע in order to cancel the gift.

keyTerms.meaning: A person on his deathbed, who can take back his gift if he recovers
Healthy
Proof

phrases.english: Mishnah:
If he did not write in it that he was on his deathbed,
and he says, "I was on my deathbed,"
and they say, "You were healthy"
phrases.notes: 'They' are the people who received the gift.

phrases.english: he must bring proof
that he was on his deathbed,
these are the words of Rabbi Meir.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new משנה and a new topic, after the story about רבא ended.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to רבי מאיר, the giver must prove he was a שכיב מרע.

steps.title: The חכמים say the burden of proof is on the one trying to take
steps.stepSummary: The חכמים disagree with רבי מאיר. Whoever wants to take property from someone else must bring the proof.
steps.simpleTranslation: The חכמים say: Whoever wants to take from his fellow must bring the proof.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה gives the opposing view of the חכמים on the same case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The חכמים use the general rule of המוציא מחבירו עליו הראיה. The giver still holds the property, so the receivers are the ones trying to take it. They must prove he was healthy, or he keeps it.

keyTerms.meaning: Whoever wants to take from another person must bring proof
The Sages, the majority view

phrases.english: And the Sages say:
Whoever wants to take from his fellow must bring the proof.
phrases.notes: Here the giver still holds the property, so the people who received the gift have to prove their claim.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the opposing view to רבי מאיר in the same משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The receivers, who want to take the property, must prove the giver was healthy.
steps.confusionAlert: Don't mix up who is trying to take. The property is still with the giver, so the receivers are the ones trying to take it, not the giver.
steps.whatToRemember: רבי מאיר says the giver must prove he was sick. The חכמים say the receivers must prove he was healthy, because they are the ones trying to take.

steps.title: A deed that mentions the illness but not that he died from it
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings a case of a deed that said the giver was sick in bed. It left out the usual line saying he died from that illness.
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: There was a certain gift document in which was written: 'When he was sick and lying in his bed.' But it did not say: 'And from his sickness he departed to his eternal home.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא sets up a real case connected to the משנה. It is preparing the question of what happens when part of the standard wording is missing.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The deed proves he was sick when he gave the gift. But it is missing the usual line showing he never recovered. That leaves room to claim he got better, which would cancel a שכיב מרע's gift. The question is how much weight to give the missing line.

keyTerms.meaning: Sick and lying in his bed
His eternal home, meaning the grave
A gift, or the document recording a gift

phrases.english: Gemara:
There was a certain gift document in which was written:
"When he was sick and lying in his bed";
but it was not written in it:
"And from his sickness he departed to his eternal home."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins the גמרא on the משנה with a real case about wording in a deathbed gift document.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Sets up the case: the deed shows he was sick but does not show he died from that illness.
